title: 1960, the Year of Africa
summary: In 1960 seventeen African countries gained independence, most from France and Britain, beginning with Cameroon on 1 January 1960. Togo, Madagascar, the Congo, Somalia, Nigeria and Mauritania were among them, and the year is remembered as the Year of Africa.

as_recorded.value: a full 17 countries gained their independence (1960); Cameroon independent from France on January 1, 1960
seventeen nations gained independence in 1960, mostly from France and Britain; Nigeria October 1, Mauritania November 28

where.modern_name: Cameroon (representative site; the process spans the African continent)
where.historical_name: Cameroon, independent from France on 1 January 1960

importance.justification: Seventeen countries changed status in one year, the largest single-year wave of African independence in the sources.
